The problem

Buildings rarely fail inside a trade. They fail between trades.

The electrician arrives after the walls are plastered. The AC duct meets a beam nobody told the HVAC vendor about. A leak at the sunken slab becomes an argument between the plumber and the tiler. Each contractor did their job. The building still lost a month.

Coordination is the recurring cause. Studies of Indian building projects keep finding the same factors near the top of the delay list: poor site coordination, weak communication between parties, and rework from mistakes made in the field.

The owner becomes the project manager. With separate contracts, every interface between trades is a decision only the owner can make, usually by phone, usually late.

Rework is paid twice. Once to break what was built, once to build it again, and the schedule absorbs both.

What turnkey means at KRS

One point of accountability, from concept to keys.

Turnkey is not a bigger contract. It is a different allocation of risk: the interfaces between trades become our problem, planned on drawings before they become your problem on site.

01

One team, every trade

Civil, plumbing, electrical, HVAC, interiors and finishing managed by a single team, so the coordination burden is ours, not the owner's.

02

In-house expertise

Hands-on experience across every major trade in a build. Problems are caught by people who have done the work, which reduces rework and delay.

03

Milestones you can see

Transparent communication, defined milestones and responsive support after handover. You always know which stage the building is in.

04

Bengaluru, locally

Headquartered in the city and familiar with local approvals, suppliers and site conditions, including the paperwork that has changed under the Greater Bengaluru Authority.

          Delivery

          The coordination tax

          KRS ENGINEERS AND CONTRACTORS · INSIGHTS

          Ask an owner why their building ran late and you will usually hear about a single trade: the electrician who did not turn up, the tiles that arrived in the wrong shade. Ask the research and you get a different answer.

          A widely cited analysis of Indian construction projects by researchers working with IIT Delhi grouped the causes of delay into a handful of underlying factors. Alongside lack of commitment and inefficient site management sat poor site coordination, lack of communication and unclear project scope. Among the variables that most affected overall delay were slow decisions by the owner and rework caused by mistakes during construction.

          A 2024 study of real estate projects in Gujarat reached a similar place by a different route. Of the seven delay factors it extracted, the first was poor stakeholder coordination. And a 2026 review of fifteen years of Indian delay research concluded that better stakeholder coordination and integrated planning are central to improving delivery.

          The pattern is consistent: delay lives in the interfaces, and the interfaces belong to whoever holds the contracts.

          Who pays for the gaps

          When an owner hires six contractors, each one is responsible for their own scope and nobody is responsible for where those scopes meet. That job falls to the owner by default. Every clash between a duct and a beam, every wall that has to be chased open for conduit, every argument about whose leak it is, becomes a decision the owner has to make, often without the technical background to make it quickly. Slow owner decisions are themselves a recognised cause of delay, so the arrangement feeds itself.

          What turnkey changes, and what it does not

          Integrated delivery moves the interfaces inside one organisation. US research by the Construction Industry Institute found that integrated design-build projects outperformed traditional separate contracts on cost, schedule, changes and rework. That is a different market, and the result should not be read as a guarantee here.

          There is also an honest counterpoint. A study of forty projects found the time advantage of integrated delivery was clear, but concluded that the contractor's project management expertise and experience may matter more than the delivery method itself. We agree. A single contract only helps if the team holding it knows every trade well enough to plan the interfaces before they reach site. That is the part of turnkey we take most seriously.

          Sources: Doloi, Sawhney, Iyer and Rentala, "Analysing factors affecting delays in Indian construction projects", International Journal of Project Management (2012). · Patel, An Empirical Study on the Delays in Construction Projects in India, Nirma University (2024) · Patil and Nagarajan, Critical Analysis of Project Delays in Building Construction Sector in the Indian Context, CTFC 2025 (2026) · An Analysis of Design/Build vs. Design-Bid-Build, citing Construction Industry Institute research · Comparative analysis of 40 design/build and design/bid/build projects
          Engineering

          Draw the services before you pour

          KRS ENGINEERS AND CONTRACTORS · INSIGHTS

          Concrete is unforgiving. Once a slab is cast, every pipe that should have passed through it, every conduit that should have been embedded in it and every opening an AC drain needed has either been accounted for or will be fought for with a core cutter.

          On a building where the services are designed and contracted separately from the structure, this is where most rework begins. The plumbing consultant draws a riser where the structural engineer drew a beam. The HVAC vendor sizes a duct for a ceiling void that the beam drop has already eaten. Nobody is wrong in their own drawing. The drawings were simply never laid on top of each other.

          The cheapest place to resolve a clash is on paper. The most expensive is after the shuttering comes off.

          How we sequence it

          In our turnkey approach, architectural, civil, electrical, plumbing and HVAC drawings are aligned before execution begins. That alignment is what allows plumbing, electrical and HVAC to be installed in parallel with structural progress, rather than waiting for the frame to finish and then working around it.

          In practice that means sleeves and inserts placed before the pour, conduit routed in the slab rather than chased into finished walls, sunken areas for wet rooms drawn with their waterproofing and falls already decided, and ceiling voids sized against the actual beam depths. Each of these is a small decision. Taken together they are the difference between a building that is finished and one that is repaired before it is occupied.

          A question worth asking any contractor

          Before you sign, ask to see how the services drawings will be checked against the structural drawings, and who is responsible when they disagree. If the answer is that each contractor will sort it out on site, the owner is the one who will be sorting it out.

          Bengaluru

          Building in Bengaluru after the GBA

          KRS ENGINEERS AND CONTRACTORS · INSIGHTS · NOVEMBER 2026

          For most of the last two decades, a building owner in the city dealt with the BBMP. That is no longer the structure. The state government dissolved the unified BBMP and replaced it with the Greater Bengaluru Authority, splitting the city into five corporations to decentralise administration. The new corporations presented their first budgets in March 2026.

          For anyone planning a build, the practical effect is that the authority, the portal and in some cases the rules have shifted, and the transition has not been frictionless. In June 2026, Deccan Herald reported a widespread approval logjam at the GBA and the Urban Development Department that left parts of the real estate sector waiting.

          The paperwork that now comes first

          Since July 2025, an e-khata has been mandatory for building licence, plinth and occupancy certificate applications on the Greater Bengaluru Authority portal. Building plan approval remains mandatory before construction starts, and guidance aimed at homeowners notes that incomplete applications are one of the most common reasons approvals are delayed.

          A realistic start date is set by the approvals file, not by the contractor's availability.

          What we suggest owners do

          Before fixing a start date, confirm which authority your plot falls under, especially in areas recently brought into Greater Bengaluru. Get the e-khata in order early. Have survey and ownership documents ready, and treat the sanctioned plan as the baseline for everything that follows, because deviations from it carry their own consequences later at the occupancy stage.

          Rules in this area are changing through 2026, so verify current requirements with the relevant authority or your architect before you apply. As a Bengaluru-headquartered contractor, we work through these steps with clients as part of planning, so the construction schedule is built on an approvals timeline that is real.

          Sources: The News Minute, Bengaluru GBA Budget: Roads, welfare, khata reforms in focus (March 2026) · Deccan Herald, Approval logjam leaves Bengaluru real estate sector in limbo (June 2026) · JSW One Homes, Home construction approvals and permissions in Bengaluru
